explanation: The DNA double helix features the sugar-phosphate backbones on the outside of the molecule, while the nitrogenous bases point inward toward the center, forming the 'rungs' or 'steps' of the helical staircase. The bases on opposite strands face each other and form hydrogen bonds, which hold the two strands of the DNA molecule together. The pairing is highly specific: Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T), forming two hydrogen bonds between them. Guanine (G) always pairs with Cytosine (C), forming three hydrogen bonds.

questions.q: How many hydrogen bonds form between Guanine (G) and Cytosine (C) in a DNA molecule?
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide states 'Guanine (G) always pairs with Cytosine (C) - Forms 3 hydrogen bonds.' Adenine and Thymine pair with 2 hydrogen bonds (Option B).
